A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same output-label privacy and continual-learning research despite the changed title. Their main texts, appendices, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison. V5 explicitly acknowledges one unfilled result cell in Table A4; this is a reporting gap rather than unavailable PDF material.

before.justification: V4 reports original classification, forgetting, label-space and blurry-task experiments in Section 7 and Appendices E–F.

after.justification: V5 retains original benchmark results and reports additional label-release, privacy-budget and baseline-comparison experiments in Section 6 and Appendices D–F.

M1.justification: V4 already provides a generic binary-mechanism construction and Laplace-threshold example for releasing labels in Appendix C.4. V5 adds a calibrated truncated symmetric geometric selector adapted from private partition selection, explicitly defining and using it before classifier training (Section 4.2, Equation 7). This is a substantial new label-selection component; the underlying Cosine Classifier and PEFT Ensemble procedures remain substantially unchanged.

E1.justification: Split-CIFAR-100, Split-ImageNet-R and 5-Datasets remain evaluated, with 5-Datasets retained in v5 Appendix F. V5 drops the distinct stochastic, imbalanced Si-Blurry scenario evaluated in v4 Section 7.2 and Table A4, while retaining i-Blurry.

E2.justification: V5 adds an enhanced implementation of Desai et al. (2021) as an evaluated DP-CL competitor on the same ViT-B/PEFT backbone (Figure 3, Appendix D.4); v4 only discusses that work. This substantially extends comparison beyond the Naive and Non-CL reference baselines. The Non-CL reference also disappears from the blurry-task comparison, although it remains elsewhere; Label Oracle and Base Dataset largely correspond to v4's existing exact-match and all-label conditions.

E3.justification: V5 introduces a search over privacy-budget allocation between label release and classifier training, plus a new Desai comparison with specified memory buffers, Poisson sampling and privacy accounting. Its i-Blurry evaluation uses 50 disjoint classes and a 10–100% blurry-sample-ratio sweep, replacing v4's coarse comparison. The previously reported 100× additional-label condition is omitted. These are new or revised evaluation designs, not evidence that all retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V5 adds sensitivity analyses linking label-release budget to accuracy and retained class counts (Figure 5, Tables A4–A5), and examines interactions between blurriness, privacy strength and label-selection method (Figure 7, Table A7). These substantially extend v4's public-label robustness and coarse blurry-task analyses. Existing ensemble-aggregation and domain-shift analyses are largely retained.

E5.justification: V4 reports min/median/max curves and mean ± standard deviation in its label-space tables. V5 uses medians with second/fourth-best seed values for several main figures and Tables A3–A7. The five-repeat primary design remains; retained benchmark tables and several figures preserve their earlier reporting conventions. This changes uncertainty presentation without establishing an increase in runs.

E6.justification: V5 adds Desai comparison results and substantial empirical results for private label release. For example, Table A7 reports Cosine Classifier median accuracy falling from 78.6% to 44.2% as the blurry ratio rises from 10% to 100% with Release Labels at epsilon = 1. V4 did not report this label-release experiment. Standard benchmark values in v4 Tables A5–A7 remain unchanged in v5 Tables A8–A10; changed mean-versus-median summaries should not be interpreted as performance gains.

T1.justification: V4 Definition 5.1 defines task-wise DP through separate per-task inequalities. V5 Definitions 3.2–3.4 instead formalize sequence adjacency, privacy of joint outputs and task assignment, followed by the new equivalence theorem, Theorem 3.5. Appendix B adds explicit higher-order task adjacency and substantially rewrites composition arguments. These are substantive mathematical revisions, beyond relocating the retained output-label leakage and remapping proofs.

C1.justification: The central claims about output-label leakage, two privacy-preserving alternatives and pre-trained DP-CL methods remain. V5 adds an explicit claim of label-retention optimality for its adopted selector and empirical superiority over prior DP-CL work under its stronger privacy model (abstract and Section 6.1). These extend the existing contribution rather than replacing its research objective.

C2.justification: V4's conclusion favors public prior labels while warning that private release can discard small classes. V5 develops conditional recommendations for both alternatives, explains their budget and blurriness trade-offs, and distinguishes when each classifier is preferable. Section 7 adds a budget-split heuristic, cautions against deriving it from sensitive class sizes without privacy protection, and identifies optimal budget allocation as unresolved.

D1.justification: V5 adds detailed implementation and accounting information for the Desai baseline, runtime-scaling discussion, and a completed ImageNet-R split description (Appendix D). Section 8 provides a source-code repository pointer where v4 only promises release upon acceptance. Most existing framework, hyperparameter and hardware disclosures remain unchanged; the repository's availability was not externally verified.

R1.justification: V5 substantially connects the work to privacy side-channels and private partition selection, adding discussions of Debenedetti et al. (2024), Desfontaines et al. (2022), Gopi et al. (2020) and Korolova et al. (2009). It explicitly credits the adopted selector and expands distinctions concerning retained state, task information and compatibility with pre-trained models (Section 2, Table 1). This changes research positioning beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work and conclusion are extensively rewritten around privacy side-channels and choosing between label methods. Task-wise theory moves into the background, domain-shift experiments move to Appendix F, and dedicated reproducibility and LLM-usage sections are added. The narrative and document organization change substantially.

P2.justification: V5 substantially retypesets the paper, adds comparison Table 1, and introduces or redesigns the principal experimental figures and appendix tables. V4's domain-shift Figure 5 becomes v5 Figure A4, while its label-dropping lower-bound Figure 2 moves to Figure A1 alongside a new main-text mechanism-probability plot. Algorithms become full-width displays, and some supplementary plots are removed.

improvement.justification: V4 proposes two label-space solutions but empirically studies mainly public labels and lacks an evaluated prior DP-CL competitor. V5 addresses these central gaps with an explicit private selector, budget and blurriness experiments, and a documented Desai comparison (Figures 3–7, Appendix D.4), substantially strengthening the evidence behind its practical recommendations. Removing Si-Blurry and leaving one Table A4 cell unfilled reduce completeness, but these limited losses do not outweigh the central empirical gains.
